headline: Adds buttons to the admin users page to change roles and delete users, but the new actions have no admin check.
what_changed: The admin users screen now has a role dropdown (member, manager, admin) for each person.
The admin users screen now has a Delete button for each person. It asks for confirmation first, and deleting also removes that person's shifts.
The role dropdown and Delete button send their requests to a new web address the app answers. That address skips the admin check that the existing user list uses.
Nothing else in the app was changed.

risks.title: Anyone can change any user's role, including making themselves admin
risks.explanation: The new role-change address does not check whether the person asking is an admin. The existing user list does check, so this new part was missed. The sign-in check on the admin pages only runs when someone opens a page. It does not protect this address. Someone who is not an admin could send a request that makes their own account admin, and then manage everyone. Likelihood is high, since the address is reachable by anyone who knows it. Fix by adding the same admin check used on the user list to both new actions before shipping.

risks.title: Anyone can delete any user and all their shift records, with no undo
risks.explanation: The new delete address has the same missing admin check. Anyone who can reach it could delete staff accounts. Deleting an account also deletes all of that person's shifts, which the database is set up to do automatically. There is no backup step or recycle bin in this change, so the data cannot be recovered from the app. This could affect pay records and schedules. Fix by adding the admin check, and confirm that backups exist and that shift history should really be removed with the account.

risks.title: Role value is not checked, so any text can be saved as a role
risks.explanation: The dropdown only offers three roles, but the server accepts whatever text it is sent. A bad or mistyped role could be saved. The app may then treat that person as having no access, or in a way no one expects. Likelihood is low for normal use, but it is easy to avoid. Fix by allowing only member, manager and admin on the server.

questions_for_developer: Can you add the same admin check that the user list uses to the role-change and delete actions, and test that a non-admin gets refused?
Should deleting a person also delete their shift history, or should we keep shifts for pay and records and only remove the account?
Can the server accept only the three allowed roles, and reject anything else?
Do we have recent database backups, and is there a way to restore a deleted user if this is shipped by mistake?
good_news: The change is small and limited to one screen and one new address.
The delete button asks the person to confirm before anything is removed.
The existing user list already checks for an admin, so the correct pattern is already in the codebase to copy.
